CLAUDE.md - ptetools Package

Source: CLAUDE.md

Claude counterpart to AGENTS.md. This file summarizes the package for LLM agents and records project-specific conventions and architectural cautions.

Project Overview

ptetools is an R package for building panel treatment effect estimators with staggered treatment timing. Its main role is to provide reusable infrastructure for estimators that can be written as:

  1. Set up a panel data problem and decide which groups and time periods matter.
  2. Loop over group-time cells (g,t).
  3. Build the local data needed for each (g,t) comparison.
  4. Estimate a local treatment effect such as ATT(g,t).
  5. Combine local estimates into overall, group-specific, dynamic/event-study, or dose-specific parameters.
  6. Conduct inference using influence functions and multiplier bootstrap when available, otherwise empirical bootstrap.

The package is intended as a backend for other packages and methods. The README mentions ife, contdid, and parts of qte as users of this infrastructure.

GitHub: https://github.com/bcallaway11/ptetools

Core Pipeline

The central workflow is:

pte()
  -> setup_pte_fun()
  -> compute.pte()
       -> subset_fun()
       -> attgt_fun()
  -> process_att_gt() or panel_empirical_bootstrap()
  -> pte_aggte()
  -> pte_results()

The package is intentionally modular. Most new methods should plug into the pipeline by providing one or more of:

  • setup_pte_fun: prepares data, chooses glist and tlist, and returns a pte_params object.
  • subset_fun: receives the full processed data plus g and tp, and returns local data for the group-time comparison.
  • attgt_fun: receives local gt_data and returns an attgt_if or attgt_noif object.

The main exported convenience wrapper is pte_default(), which combines setup_pte, two_by_two_subset, and pte_attgt for DID/unconfoundedness-style estimators.

Key Contracts

Data Setup

setup_pte() and setup_pte_non_numeric_groups() create internal columns:

  • G: treatment group / first treatment time, or named group identifier
  • id: unit identifier
  • period: normalized time period
  • Y: outcome
  • .w: weights, defaulting to 1
  • ftt: first treated time, for non-numeric groups

Time periods are required to be positive integers. Numeric treatment groups are recoded to consecutive internal periods using BMisc::orig2t() and later mapped back with BMisc::t2orig(). Be careful when changing this logic, since it affects aggregation, event time, and display.

setup_pte_basic() is lighter and mostly serves as an example/minimal setup.

Group-Time Subsets

subset_fun must return a list with:

  • gt_data: local data, usually a gt_data_frame
  • n1: number of unique units in the local subset
  • disidx: logical/index vector mapping local influence functions back to the full set of units

gt_data_frame() expects at least the columns G, id, period, name, Y, and D, where name marks "pre" or "post" and D marks the local treated group.

Important subset functions:

  • two_by_two_subset(): canonical 2x2 pre/post treated/comparison subset.
  • keep_all_untreated_subset(): keeps untreated observations plus current group; useful for imputation-style estimators.
  • keep_all_pretreatment_subset(): keeps all data through tp for group g and not-yet-treated/never-treated comparison groups; useful for IFE-type methods.

Group-Time Estimation

attgt_fun should return:

  • attgt_if(attgt, inf_func, extra_gt_returns = NULL) when an influence function is available.
  • attgt_noif(attgt, extra_gt_returns = NULL) when no influence function is available.

If an influence function is returned, compute.pte() rescales it by n / n1 and embeds it into the full-unit influence function matrix. If no influence function is returned, or boot_type = "empirical", the package falls back to panel_empirical_bootstrap().

Built-in examples:

  • did_attgt(): DRDID-based panel DID for local 2x2 comparisons.
  • pte_attgt(): more general local ATT estimator supporting levels or first differences, pre-treatment covariates, changes in covariates, lagged outcome covariates, and est_method = "dr" or "reg".

Results And Classes

Main classes:

  • pte_params: parameter object produced by setup functions.
  • group_time_att: processed ATT(g,t) estimates with standard errors, influence functions, pre-test, and extra group-time returns.
  • pte_results: standard overall result object containing att_gt, overall_att, event_study, and ptep.
  • aggte_obj: aggregation result used for overall, group, and dynamic effects.
  • pte_emp_boot: empirical-bootstrap result object.
  • dose_obj: continuous-treatment result object.
  • named_groups: maps non-numeric groups to first-treated times.

summary() and print() methods exist for the main result classes. ggpte() plots event-study results for pte_results and group-time effects for group_time_att. ggpte_cont() plots dose-specific continuous-treatment effects.

Inference And Aggregation

process_att_gt() handles influence-function based results:

  • Builds analytical variance from the influence function matrix.
  • Uses mboot2() for multiplier-bootstrap standard errors and uniform critical values.
  • Computes a Wald pre-test for pre-treatment ATT(g,t) values when feasible.
  • Maps normalized time/group values back to the original scale.

pte_aggte() is adapted from did::aggte() and currently supports:

  • type = "group": group-specific effects and an overall ATT weighted by group size.
  • type = "dynamic": event-study effects, with optional min_e, max_e, and balance_e.

Inference for aggregated parameters includes influence-function terms for estimated group weights via wif().

Continuous And Distributional Extensions

Continuous-treatment support is partly implemented through:

  • gt_type = "dose"
  • process_dose_gt()
  • dose_obj
  • ggpte_cont()

The group-time function for dose applications is expected to put dose-specific objects such as att.d, acrt.d, bet, bread, and Xe in extra_gt_returns.

Distributional treatment effect support is only a stub:

  • process_dtt_gt() currently stops with “not implemented yet”.
  • gt_type = "dtt" in pte() is not supported yet.
  • Empirical bootstrap has branches for gt_type = "qtt" and "qott" through qtt_pte_aggregations() and qott_pte_aggregations().

tests/testthat/ DID comparison and inference tests

Dependencies

Imports include BMisc, Matrix, ggplot2, DRDID, tidyr, dplyr, pbapply, and splines2. did is in Suggests and is used heavily in tests and README examples.

Prefer base R where reasonable, but this package already uses selected tidyverse tools (dplyr, tidyr) in the bootstrap and data reshaping code. Avoid adding new dependencies unless they are clearly justified.

Known Issues And Cautions

  • The working tree may contain ongoing edits; do not revert user changes.
  • global_fun, time_period_fun, and group_fun are design hooks but are not implemented as general optimizations.
  • process_dtt_gt() and gt_type = "dtt" are stubs.
  • R/imputation_functions.R contains in-progress code with browser() and a fixest call, but fixest is not in DESCRIPTION.
  • Some empirical-bootstrap test coverage is skipped because return naming does not currently match the standard results.
  • summary.pte_emp_boot() has a hard-coded alp <- .05.
  • Many internal helper functions are exported; be cautious about changing names or return structures because downstream packages may rely on them.
  • pte_aggte() and process_att_gt() preserve compatibility with parts of the did object structure through fields such as DIDparams, c, and inffunc.

Development Commands

devtools::load_all()
devtools::document()
devtools::test()
lintr::lint_file("R/foo.R")
lintr::lint_package()
rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck()

Before broad changes, run the relevant testthat tests. For changes affecting exports or roxygen comments, run devtools::document() and check NAMESPACE and man/ changes.

Collaboration Notes

  • Follow the global R preferences in the user’s Codex instructions: prefer base R and data.table where possible, avoid unnecessary dependencies, use informative errors, and keep econometric notation clear.
  • Do not rename functions, arguments, returned list fields, S3 classes, or output column names without explicit approval and an old-to-new mapping.
  • Preserve the package’s estimator contract. New methods should usually be added by writing a focused setup, subset, or group-time estimation function rather than rewriting pte().
  • When editing existing code, maintain downstream compatibility with packages that use ptetools as a backend.
